'''Enrico Giusti''' (28 October 1940 – 26 March 2024) was an Italian mathematician mainly known for his contributions to the fields of [[calculus of variations]], regularity theory of [[partial differential equation]]s, [[minimal surfaces]] and [[history of mathematics]]. He was professor of mathematics at the [[University of Florence|Università di Firenze]];<ref name="unifi">{{cite web|url=http://www.math.unifi.it/schedapersonale?p=1187|title=Scheda Personale &#124; DiMaI - Dipartimento di Matematica e Informatica "Ulisse Dini"|publisher=math.unifi.it|accessdate=21 July 2016}}</ref> he also taught and conducted research at the [[Australian National University]] at Canberra, at the [[Stanford University]] and at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.matematicamente.it/cultura/interviste_a_matematici/intervista_a_enrico_giusti_200710081784/ |title=Intervista a Enrico Giusti &#124; per, Matematica, non, Nel &#124; Matematicamente.it |access-date=23 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927143901/http://www.matematicamente.it/cultura/interviste_a_matematici/intervista_a_enrico_giusti_200710081784/ |archive-date=27 September 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> After retirement, he devoted himself to the managing of the "Giardino di Archimede",<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://web.math.unifi.it/archimede/archimede/index.html |title=Il giardino di Archimede. Un Museo per la Matematica |access-date=23 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110826092427/http://web.math.unifi.it/archimede/archimede/index.html |archive-date=26 August 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> a museum entirely dedicated to mathematics and its applications. Giusti was also the editor-in-chief of the international journal dedicated to the history of mathematics ''Bollettino di storia delle scienze matematiche'' (''Bulletin of the history of the mathematical sciences'').<ref name="libraweb">{{cite web|url=http://www.libraweb.net/riviste.php?chiave=92|title=LibraWeb - The Online Integrated Platform of Fabrizio Serra editore, Pisa-Roma|publisher=libraweb.net|accessdate=21 July 2016}}</ref><ref name="unifi2">{{cite web|url=http://php.math.unifi.it/archimede/archimede/bollettino/bollettino.php|title=Il giardino di Archimede|publisher=php.math.unifi.it|accessdate=21 July 2016}}</ref>

One of Giusti's most famous results, obtained with [[Enrico Bombieri]] and [[Ennio De Giorgi]], concerned the minimality of [[James Harris Simons|Simons]]' cones, and made it possible to disprove the validity of [[Bernstein's problem|Bernstein's theorem]] in dimensions larger than 8. The work on minimal surfaces was mentioned in the citation of the [[Fields Medal]], eventually awarded to Bombieri in 1974.

Giusti had a sustained interest in the history of mathematics, e.g. the mathematics of [[Pierre de Fermat]] (see Giusti 2009). At the time of his death, he was the director of the [[Garden of Archimedes]], a museum devoted to mathematics in Florence, Italy.<ref>[http://www.eosdev.it/Esperienze/GiardinoArchimede/ Il Giardino Di Archimede] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222032803/http://eosdev.it/Esperienze/GiardinoArchimede/ |date=22 February 2016 }} EOS: IT solutions for the enterprise</ref>

Giusti died in Florence on 26 March 2024, at the age of 83.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lutto nel mondo scientifico: è morto il grande matematico Enrico Giusti |url=https://www.lanazione.it/cronaca/lutto-nel-mondo-scientifico-e-morto-il-grande-matematico-enrico-giusti-ruia3y2w |access-date=28 March 2024 |publisher=La Nazione |date=28 March 2024}}</ref>

==Awards==
Giusti won the [[Caccioppoli Prize]] of the [[Italian Mathematical Union]] in 1978<ref name="unibo">{{cite web|url=http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/index-en.html|title=Caccioppoli Prize|publisher=umi.dm.unibo.it|accessdate=21 July 2016|archive-date=14 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514091912/http://umi.dm.unibo.it/caccioppoli/index-en.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 2003 was awarded the national medal for mathematics by the Accademia Nazionale delle Scienze (dei XL).
